name: Siemens Energy AG
monetization: Sells gas turbines, grid technologies (transformers, HVDC, switchgear), and long-term service into AI-driven power demand; order book stretches to four-year delivery waits.
description_md: Siemens Energy is Europe's counterpart to GE Vernova across the AI power bottleneck: heavy-duty gas turbines (Gas Services), grid equipment including transformers and HVDC (Grid Technologies), industrial decarbonization, and the Siemens Gamesa wind business. AI data-center demand pushed its total order backlog to a record €154B in fiscal Q2 2026 and €162B by fiscal Q3, with the gas-turbine order book alone at ~87GW — enough to force delivery waits of up to four years. Grid Technologies, which sells the transformers and switchgear the buildout is chronically short of, carries a €51B backlog of its own.
ai_monetization_md: Monetization mirrors GE Vernova's: equipment sales gated by manufacturing capacity, price escalation on scarce slots, and multi-decade service contracts on the installed fleet. Fiscal Q3 2026 showed record orders with Grid Technologies orders of €5.4B (+28% y/y), revenue +29% to €3.6B at a 19.9% margin. The company raised annual production of medium gas turbines from ~50 units (FY2025) to ~80 (FY2026), with large-turbine capacity additions contributing from FY2027 — meaning today's demand converts to revenue over many years. FY2026 guidance: comparable revenue growth 14–16%, net income ~€4B, free cash flow ~€8B.
ai_strategy_md: Expand capacity without repeating past quality crises: measured ramp of turbine production, aggressive growth in Grid Technologies (the transformer/HVDC bottleneck), and selectivity on which data-center-driven orders to take — management openly discusses a four-year wait as a demand-shaping tool. The formerly loss-making Siemens Gamesa wind unit turned a profit in fiscal Q3 2026, removing the group's chronic drag just as the gas and grid businesses accelerate.
risk_notes_md: Same cycle risk as the rest of the turbine cluster: a four-year order book built on AI-era load forecasts faces cancellation or re-phasing risk if data-center demand disappoints — and capacity being added now would then land in a soft market. Backlog (€154–162B) is committed orders, not revenue, and includes long-dated service. Wind's recovery is one quarter old. German grid-connection and supply-chain constraints can gate how fast even a record backlog converts.

observations.notes: Fiscal Q3 = Apr–Jun 2026. Backlog set a then-record €154B in fiscal Q2 2026 before reaching €162B in Q3; AI data-center demand cited as the driver.
Order book has ballooned to ~87GW; medium gas-turbine annual production raised from ~50 units (FY2025) to ~80 (FY2026).
Lead times of up to four years for gas turbines — one of the hard physical constraints on AI data-center power.
Q3 Grid Technologies orders €5.4B (+28% y/y); revenue €3.6B (+29%); 19.9% margin before special items. Transformers/HVDC are a named buildout bottleneck.

events.title: Fiscal Q3 2026: record backlog (€162B), Gamesa turns profitable, FY outlook raised
events.why_it_matters: Confirms AI data-center demand as the driver of record orders across both turbines and grid equipment, while the wind unit's return to profit removes the group's structural drag.
